funfact_topics.text: Cows form close, lasting friendships and get stressed when separated from a preferred companion.
Bananas are naturally radioactive
Roman concrete self-heals: lime clasts react with water to reform calcium carbonate and seal cracks.
A googol (10^100) is larger than the number of atoms in the observable universe (~10^80).
The University of Oxford is older than the Aztec Empire.
Jupiter's Great Red Spot is larger than Earth
Wombats are the only animals that produce cube-shaped poop.
Cleopatra lived closer to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid.
The Eiffel Tower grows about 15 cm taller in summer
The shortest war in history, the Anglo-Zanzibar War of 1896, lasted about 38 minutes.
A teaspoon of neutron-star material would weigh about a billion tonnes.
In a room of just 23 people, there is a better-than-even chance two share a birthday.
Babies are born with about 300 bones but adults have 206
The Sahara was a green savannah with lakes as recently as about 5,000 to 11,000 years ago
Sharks are older than trees
Scotland's national animal is the unicorn.
Saturn would float in water
Flamingos are born grey and turn pink from their diet
Some red food dye (carmine/cochineal, E120) is made from crushed cochineal insects.
The first 'computer bug' was a literal moth found in Harvard's Mark II in 1947 and taped into the logbook.
The Sun holds about 99.8% of the solar system's mass.

Bubble wrap was not invented to protect packages. In 1957, engineers Alfred Fielding and Marc Chavannes sealed two shower curtains together and first tried to sell the bubbly sheet as textured wallpaper, and then as greenhouse insulation. Only later did their company, Sealed Air, market it as protective packaging — the use that made it famous.
Mauna Kea is taller than Everest measured from base to peak
The dot over i and j is called a tittle
The Hundred Years' War lasted 116 years (1337-1453), not a single continuous war nor exactly a century.
An octopus has three hearts and blue (copper-based) blood; its main systemic heart stops beating whenever it swims.
The inventor of the Pringles can was buried in one
Gallium is a metal that melts in your hand (m.p. ~29.8 C) yet has one of the longest liquid ranges of any element.
There are more trees on Earth (~3 trillion) than stars in the Milky Way (~100-400 billion).
Canada has more lakes than the rest of the world combined
The word 'robot' comes from Karel Capek's 1920 play R.U.R., from Czech 'robota' (forced labour); his brother Josef coined it.
Honey is one of the very few foods that essentially never spoils. Its low moisture content, high acidity, and the trace hydrogen peroxide produced by bee enzyme
A single bolt of lightning is about five times hotter than the Sun's surface (~30,000 C vs ~5,500 C).
Nintendo was founded in 1889 as a hanafuda playing-card maker in Kyoto, decades before it made video games.
You are taller in the morning than at night; spinal discs compress under gravity through the day and rebound overnight.
There are about 8x10^67 (52!) ways to arrange a 52-card deck, so any well shuffle is almost certainly unique in history.
Antarctica is the largest desert on Earth; its interior is drier than the Sahara.
Sudan has more pyramids than Egypt
Tardigrades are the only animals known to have survived the open vacuum of space (2007 ESA FOTON-M3 experiment).
Under the 1667 Treaty of Breda the Dutch kept the tiny nutmeg island of Run and handed Manhattan to England.
Hot water can sometimes freeze faster than cold (the Mpemba effect)
Helium was discovered on the Sun before it was ever found on Earth. In 1868 astronomers Pierre Janssen and Norman Lockye
The word 'quarantine' comes from the Venetian quaranta giorni (forty days), the ship isolation period used in Black Death Venice.
Sea otters raft together and wrap in kelp (or hold paws) while sleeping to avoid drifting apart on the current.
The largest living organism on Earth is a honey fungus (Armillaria ostoyae) in Oregon's Blue Mountains, spanning about 9.6 sq km and estimated to be up to roughly 8,650 years old.
Point Nemo is so remote the nearest humans are often astronauts in orbit
Pluto has not completed a single orbit around the Sun since its 1930 discovery; its orbital period is about 248 years.
Butterflies taste with their feet via chemoreceptors on their tarsi.
Carrots were originally purple, white or yellow; the orange carrot was bred by Dutch growers, first recorded in 1721, and gets its colour from beta-carotene.
The world’s first webcam was created in 1991 to watch the Trojan Room coffee pot at the University of Cambridge.
Scorpions glow blue-green under ultraviolet light because compounds in their exoskeleton, including beta-carboline, fluoresce; field researchers hunt them at ni
A day on Venus is longer than its year: it rotates once in about 243 Earth days but orbits the Sun in about 225.
